transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Emily Castillo (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jon Park (TidalCare CTO), Lina Gomez (Head of Ops), Ravi Shah (Security)

Summary:
Quick kickoff-style intake focusing on implementation constraints, security requirements, and pilot success criteria. SE to run perf bench; CSM to send onboarding & SOC2 artifacts; security deep-dive scheduled.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and success metrics
- Private vs. hosted deployment options and VPC connectivity
- SOC2/SAML/KMS expectations and audit log needs
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and burst capacity

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Emily Castillo: hey everyone thanks for joining, we, um, wanted to do a quick intake so we can line up the pilot and security deep dive. is this still a good time for you all?
[00:00:12] Jon Park: yeah good, thanks emily. we have about an hour, so great. quick context: TidalCare's building a triage assistant for intake nurses, so latency and PII handling are key.
[00:00:27] Lina Gomez: and just to add, ops needs to know how the rollout will look — we have nightly batch jobs and live chat flows.
[00:00:36] Marcus Lee: perfect. i'll be the SE on this, i'll try to get as technical as possible — i know you mentioned both live low-latency and batch use cases, right?
[00:00:45] Jon Park: correct, live chat must be snappy; target 95th percentile under 300 ms ideally, but we can relax in pilot. batch is for summarization and embeddings overnight.
[00:00:58] Ravi Shah: from security, SOC2 is mandatory for our vendor list. we also need SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration, and audit logs retained for 1 year. any of that a hard no?
[00:01:12] Marcus Lee: for sure, we support SAML and RBAC, KMS integration is available for Private deployments and also for Dedicated depending on your key policy. audit logs — we can route them to your SIEM, retention adjustable.
[00:01:30] Jon Park: when you say Private, do you mean on-prem? or VPC-hosed? we have a locked-down VPC and we can't open the egress on some nodes.
[00:01:41] Marcus Lee: Private includes VPC peering or private link style connectivity, and there is an on-prem package we can discuss. there may be some kernel-level performance tradeoffs on air-gapped on-prem but functionally it's supported.
[00:01:56] Lina Gomez: another constraint: data residency — any patient data must stay in us-east-1. can we pin region?
[00:02:04] Emily Castillo: yes region pinning is supported, we can route traffic and set model variants to run in specific regions. we'll need the list of subnets and allowed CIDR to propose a peering plan.
[00:02:16] Jon Park: okay we'll get that.
[00:02:20] Marcus Lee: on the perf side, do you have a sense of average sequence length and token rates? that'll inform batching and model choice.
[00:02:29] Lina Gomez: average prompts are ~120 tokens, but summaries can jump to 600+ tokens for discharge notes.
[00:02:36] Marcus Lee: got it. for that mix i might suggest a 13B quantized variant for cost balance or a 7B with longer context if you need more throughput. we can bench both.
[00:02:48] Ravi Shah: cost is a big concern, but not at the expense of data control. also vendor lock-in worry — what sort of exportability is there for models and logs?
[00:02:58] Marcus Lee: logs and artifacts are exportable; model versions you pin and you can snapshot prompts and eval sets. if you go Private you manage the infra so export is trivial. for hosted we provide data export instances on request.
[00:03:12] Jon Park: what about KV cache stuff? we read a note saying 'K-V cash' in a doc and it sounded odd — how does that affect stateful chat?
[00:03:22] Marcus Lee: yes, KV cache — sorry the docs sometimes say K-V cash — it's key-value cache. it's used to persist token cache for chat so subsequent calls are cheap. for cross-instance caching we'll need a shared redis or our built-in cache if you use Dedicated.
[00:03:36] Emily Castillo: i'll drop the caching doc link in the follow-up.
[00:03:40] [00:03:40] (brief crosstalk)
[00:03:55] Marcus Lee: security question: are you expecting our keys in your KMS or ours? we support both.
[00:04:03] Ravi Shah: prefer customer-managed KMS, HSM-backed, FIPS if possible. any constraints?
[00:04:10] Marcus Lee: that's supported in Private and in Dedicated with the right contract. Hosted has managed keys by default but we can enable CMEK for enterprise customers.
[00:04:20] Jon Park: ok great. next on pilot: timeline wise we're aiming to pilot in 6 weeks, prod in Q3. is that realistic?
[00:04:30] Marcus Lee: 6 weeks is tight but achievable for a narrow pilot — we'll scope the MVP to a small set of intents and user flows. benching and security review will be the gating items.
[00:04:42] Lina Gomez: who's typically involved from your side for the pilot?
[00:04:46] Emily Castillo: CSM (me) and SE (marcus) plus solutions engineering support and an onboarding engineer. we'll also bring in a security engineer for compliance sign-off.
[00:04:57] Jon Park: ok. any blockers you foresee?
[00:05:00] Marcus Lee: network connectivity is the usual one; also sample data access for benching. if you can't share real PII, synthetic data with similar token distribution is fine.
[00:05:11] Ravi Shah: we can provision a sanitized dump for benching. will you need full data schema or just samples?
[00:05:17] Marcus Lee: samples plus schema are ideal.
[00:05:21] [00:05:21] Emily Castillo: quick pause — i put a short intake form in the meeting chat (link: https://redwood.ai/onboarding/intake/tidalcare). please fill that asap.
[00:05:33] Jon Park: saw it, will do.
[00:05:36] Marcus Lee: on observability — you'll get per-route token breakdowns, latencies, and cost estimates. if you want tracing into your app we can add headers to pass trace IDs.
[00:05:48] Lina Gomez: audit logs detail — can we get a sample log schema? we need to show it to our compliance team.
[00:05:55] Marcus Lee: yes i'll attach the log schema in the follow-up.
[00:05:59] [00:05:59] (short pause)
[00:06:10] Jon Park: about rollouts — do you support canary and automatic fallback? we want a safe rollout for new prompt configs.
[00:06:17] Marcus Lee: yes canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant on error or latency spike. rollouts are configurable per-route.
[00:06:29] Ravi Shah: on logging, any PII redaction at the platform level? we want to avoid storing PHI in raw logs.
[00:06:38] Marcus Lee: we offer prompt redaction and can obfuscate or drop certain fields before logging. we recommend client-side redaction combined with server-side policies for defense in depth.
[00:06:50] Emily Castillo: ok we're about 6 minutes in, maybe we should map next steps and owners.
[00:06:57] Marcus Lee: agreed. i'll run two benches — 7B and 13B quantized — with your sample and synthetic data if needed. i'll also try to simulate 50 concurrent users to approximate production load.
[00:07:09] Jon Park: that'd be great. also can you include a cost estimate for both variants?
[00:07:15] Marcus Lee: yes cost per 1k tokens and per-concurrent-user estimate.
[00:07:20] [00:07:20] (brief typing/silence)
[00:07:45] Lina Gomez: procurement question: do you have standard BAAs for healthcare? we need HIPAA considerations.
[00:07:52] Emily Castillo: we do have a BAA addendum for enterprise plans; i'll flag legal to send the template.
[00:08:00] Ravi Shah: and will there be a security questionnaire or SIG? we typically send an A3 security packet.
[00:08:06] Emily Castillo: yes we'll accept your SIG; Marcus will coordinate with our security engineer to fill out or provide evidence.
[00:08:15] Jon Park: ok. anything else re: infra?
[00:08:20] Marcus Lee: just one note — for low-latency you might want reserved capacity (Dedicated) if you need predictable p95 under 300 ms. Hosted can get close but there's more variability.
[00:08:33] Jon Park: budget-wise, what order of magnitude are we talking?
[00:08:36] Marcus Lee: rough ballpark depends on tokens and concurrency; for small pilot — think a few thousand dollars a month; for production with reserved capacity could be five figures. i'll put concrete numbers in the follow-up spreadsheet.
[00:08:49] Lina Gomez: ok we'll evaluate.
[00:08:52] [00:08:52] (crosstalk, laughter)
[00:09:05] Marcus Lee: any compliance certs beyond SOC2? we list ISO as well on the docs page but if you need FedRAMP or HITRUST that's a longer discussion.
[00:09:15] Ravi Shah: SOC2 and HIPAA are our immediate needs. HITRUST not required yet.
[00:09:22] Emily Castillo: noted. i'll include SOC2 attachments.
[00:09:27] Jon Park: what about model eval — we need to ensure no hallucinations on medication names. can you run evals on our prompt set?
[00:09:36] Marcus Lee: yes we run evals and can configure guardrails, chains of thought controls, and structured output validators. we can also do reranking for sensitive entities.
[00:09:48] Lina Gomez: any sample of structured output config?
[00:09:52] Marcus Lee: i'll share a sample json schema and a small repo example.
[00:09:58] [00:09:58] (pause)
[00:10:10] Jon Park: proposal for pilot scope — 3 intents for triage, 1 summarization flow for discharge notes, integrated with our EHR mock. is that reasonable?
[00:10:21] Emily Castillo: that sounds perfect as an MVP. we can map acceptance criteria: intent accuracy thresholds, latency, and no PHI leakage in logs.
[00:10:31] Marcus Lee: i'll set up a small test harness to run synthetic traffic and capture metrics.
[00:10:36] Ravi Shah: i want to see what the audit trail looks like when staff edit generated content. do you capture edit events?
[00:10:44] Marcus Lee: yes we can capture interaction events and link them to user IDs if you pass them; we can also store diffs of generated vs final text if you want.
[00:10:54] Jon Park: how long to get a POC environment?
[00:10:58] Emily Castillo: after we get intake form and network details, we can spin up a test environment in 1-2 weeks, benching can happen in parallel.
[00:11:08] [00:11:08] (short silence)
[00:11:20] Marcus Lee: one more technical note: quantization can reduce memory but might slightly change outputs. we'll include eval regressions so you can see quality delta.
[00:11:33] Lina Gomez: understood.
[00:11:36] Jon Park: ok wrap-up?
[00:11:39] Emily Castillo: recap — Marcus runs benches and shares cost spreadsheet; Marcus shares log schema and small repo examples; Emily to send SOC2 and onboarding checklist; Ravi to send network diagram and KMS policy; Jon to confirm stakeholders and fill intake form.
[00:11:56] Marcus Lee: i'll propose 2026-04-20 10am PT for the technical deep dive — does that work for you?
[00:12:05] Jon Park: works for me. Lina?
[00:12:08] Lina Gomez: works.
[00:12:10] Emily Castillo: i'll send invites after the call.
[00:12:14] [00:12:14] (meeting moves to Q&A, small asides)
[00:20:00] Jon Park: (later) can you show a quick example of the rollout UI?
[00:20:07] Marcus Lee: yes — describing: it's a per-route setting in console, you can set canary weights and fallback models, and enable tracing. (UI described, slight transcription artifacts)
[00:30:00] Lina Gomez: (later) procurement ask: can we get a sample contract term sheet?
[00:30:08] Emily Castillo: we'll send a sample term sheet and BAA template.
[00:40:00] Marcus Lee: (later) note: if you want on-prem package, the lead time is longer — typically 6-8 weeks to provision and validate air-gapped installs.
[00:50:00] Ravi Shah: (later) can you indicate what logs include IPs? we prefer hashed IPs if possible.
[00:50:10] Marcus Lee: hashing is doable, we support pseudonymization. i'll call that out in the log schema.
[00:57:00] Emily Castillo: great, thanks everyone — we'll send the follow-ups and action items. speak soon.

End of transcript.
